subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw refresh and land the bounded provider tool-schema normalization cache now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated source-level work is clear, but the permanent boundary affects provider hooks, custom provider behavior, plugin metadata lifecycle, and the prepared-runtime migration direction.

options.title: Refresh the bounded cache
options.body: Refresh or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 so known bundled normalizers can cache cloned schema parameters while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to avoid a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini live proof or heap evidence confirms the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Refresh the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 so known bundled normalizers can cache cloned schema parameters while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice intersects the prepared-runtime migration tracker and the provider/runtime boundary that mcaxtr is already coordinating.
